options.content:
**Story:** read top → bottom: *is it up?* → *how much work?* → *how fast?* → *does load move the hardware?* → *which resources / clients?*  
**Colours:** Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe palette; series also differ by dash pattern + point markers, so they remain readable in greyscale / print / PDF.  
**Scales:** linear unless the axis label says *log*. Units are in every axis label. Refresh 5 s; scrape 5 s; rates use 1 m windows.  
**Legend colours:** *single* = blue solid, *bulk* = orange dashed (consistent across panels).

panels.title: 1 · Application health — is it up, busy, failing?
App status
panels.description: 1 if Prometheus can scrape the Streamlit app's /metrics, else 0.

panels.title: Host status
panels.description: node_exporter reachability (needed for the correlation panels).

panels.title: Images processed · last 1 h
panels.description: Successful captions in the last hour (counter increase).

panels.title: Error ratio · 5 m
panels.description: Failed images ÷ all images over 5 m. Orange > 1 %, vermilion > 10 %.

panels.title: p95 inference · 5 m
panels.description: 95th percentile per-image inference time over 5 m (from histogram buckets).

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Submissions being processed right now (gauge).

panels.title: Image throughput · by mode
panels.description:
Successful captions per minute, split by single vs bulk. Bulk bursts dominate load.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Submissions · by mode
panels.description:
How many uploads users made per minute (a ZIP counts once).

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Errors · by type
panels.description:
Failures per minute by cause. Flat zero = healthy.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Cumulative images · stacked
panels.description:
Running total of captioned images since the app started (monotonic counter).

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Inference latency percentiles · p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description:
Time to caption one image. p99 ≫ p50 means a heavy tail (large images, CPU contention). Log axis spreads the tail.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: p95 inference by mode · by mode
panels.description:
Does bulk (sustained back-to-back load) slow each image compared with single uploads?

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Mean inference (Summary) · from _sum/_count
panels.description:
Average = rate(_sum) ÷ rate(_count) from the Summary metric — cheap and exact, but cannot be aggregated into percentiles.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: End-to-end p95 · p95, 5 m window
panels.description:
Whole submission time: a 40-image ZIP takes tens of seconds, so this is the user-visible wait.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Inference-time distribution · heatmap
panels.description: Each column is one minute; rows are latency buckets (seconds, log-spaced); brighter = more images. Shows bimodal behaviour that percentiles hide. Colour scale (Cividis) is colour-blind safe.

panels.title: 4 · Correlation — does application load move the hardware?
Host CPU vs bulk throughput · node_exporter vs app
panels.description:
Left axis: whole-machine CPU busy %. Right axis: bulk images/min. CPU climbing right after throughput confirms inference is CPU-bound.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Host memory vs app memory · node_exporter vs app
panels.description:
Left: host RAM used %. Right: the app process's resident memory (model weights + activations). Steps in RSS explain host-RAM steps.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Load average vs active requests · node_exporter vs app
panels.description:
1-minute load average (runnable tasks) against concurrent submissions. Load > core count = queueing.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Disk busy vs bulk throughput · node_exporter vs app
panels.description:
Busiest disk's I/O utilisation against bulk images/min: reading ZIP members and writing temp files.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: App process memory · gauge
panels.description:
Resident memory of the Streamlit process (BLIP-base ≈ 1–2 GB). A steady upward drift would indicate a leak.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: App process CPU · gauge
panels.description:
CPU used by the app process; 100 % = one full core, can exceed 100 % with multi-threaded torch.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Concurrency · gauges
panels.description:
Requests in flight by mode, plus images still queued in the running bulk job.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Payload profile · Summary _sum/_count
panels.description:
Mean uploaded image size (left, from Summary) and mean caption length in words (right).

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Host CPU · all cores
panels.description:
Share of CPU time not idle, all cores averaged.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Host memory · host
panels.description:
RAM in use = 1 − available ÷ total.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Root disk · mountpoint /
panels.description:
Used space on the root filesystem.

X-axis: wall-clock time (linear).

panels.title: Top clients · images captioned in the last hour
panels.description: Per-client and per-session usage from the client_ip / session_id labels. Use it to spot who is driving a bulk spike. High-cardinality labels: fine for a lab, risky in production.
